summary: The note reports on a set of park and playground renovation projects across a city, launched after September 1, 2023. Projects include Centennial Park, Children's Corner, the Greenwood Project, the Old Oak Tree Playground and Echo Park, blending historic preservation with modern features. Funding comes from community fundraising and a grant from the Harold and Beatrice Williams Foundation, matched with city park funds.
one_line: Several city parks and playgrounds are being renovated in 2023, funded by a foundation grant and city funds, combining local history with modern design.
key_facts: The revitalization of neighborhood parks and playgrounds is described as underway after September 1, 2023.
Centennial Park, on the East Side, will be restored; its historical bandstand will be repainted and fortified as a centerpiece for future concerts and gatherings.
Councilman Edward Thompson and Parks and Recreation Director Maria Sanchez unveiled the Centennial Park blueprints.
Children's Corner in West Park will replace aging metal structures with a nature-inspired playground echoing the original 1950s landscape designs.
Lead designer Robert Wu detailed the Children's Corner plans, which include eco-friendly materials and inclusive equipment for children of all abilities.
The Greenwood Project, in the southern part of the city, is led by local historian and technologist Dr. Amanda Li and uses augmented reality to bring park history to life.
Greenwood Project visitors can use smartphones to see historical reenactments, access interactive timelines, and learn about local flora and fauna.
The Old Oak Tree Playground in North Heights is home to the city's oldest living oak tree, more than two centuries old.
The new Old Oak Tree Playground will feature treehouse platforms connected by bridges.
A substantial grant from the Harold and Beatrice Williams Foundation was secured, matching contributions from the city's fund for park enhancements.
Echo Park's refurbished unveiling is scheduled for late October 2023, with a grand opening ceremony featuring historical reenactors and modern play sculptures.
